title: [human] spec 15.2 key-storage MUST (secure element / flash readout protection) vs plain-flash implementations in all stacks
description: Human adjudication needed (sweep part 3, R-06-341, docs/spec-coverage/06-security-part3-flagged.md A4). spec/06-security.md L1211-1216: 'Private keys MUST be stored in: hardware secure element (preferred), flash with readout protection, never transmitted over the air'. Implemented reality: never-over-the-air holds everywhere (no private-key TX path). Storage is plain flash with integrity only - C identity_store.c (LIKY record, CRC, mutex, settings rollback authority), Rust lichend.rs:166-236 (Zeroizing, abort on unreadable/persist-fail), Python key_persistence.py (0600 two-slot, docstring cites 15.2). No SE/ATECC/RDP support anywhere (grep zero hits). Tension: the project threat model (AGENTS.md) explicitly excludes physical/cold-boot attackers - the ONLY adversary that SE/RDP defends against; per project rules these defenses must not be demanded in reviews. Options: (a) amend 15.2 to match threat model ('stored in flash; never transmitted; secure element preferred where hardware provides it') - mirrors GUARD_PPM-style align-spec precedents; (b) keep the MUST as hardware-deployment guidance and accept code divergence. Mark decides; do not plan a code fix until adjudicated.
